In the time before memory, two siblings discovered the world's first grain seeds. The Elder Sister found them growing wild on the mountainside, while the Younger Brother learned the secret of cultivation from watching the birds.

The Elder Sister came to her brother with a proposal: "I will give you half my seeds if you promise to share your knowledge of planting. Together, we can feed our people through the coming winter."

From that day forward, their people learned: trust given freely multiplies like grain in good soil, but trust withheld leaves everyone hungry.

From that day forward, the rivers taught the people below: **Trust is the spring from which abundance flows. Those who give may risk loss, but those who honor trust multiply prosperity for all.**

The villages prospered for generations, guided by the wisdom of the Twin Rivers.
